unresolved: No Atlantic-specific site inventory is cited by this three-paper synopsis, so its blanket assertion of no pre-14 ka coastal complexes is not accepted as a demonstrated negative finding.
Lack of confirmation is not refutation. The Atlantic question remains to be evaluated against regional archaeological and palaeoshoreline evidence.
Do not infer that all early coastal travel required a single specialized toolkit; diagnostic criteria in one proposed model are not universal proof requirements.
corrections: All three cited studies concern Pacific contexts; the synopsis overextends their scope to Atlantic Canada.
The synopsis has only three sources and itself states that the consensus meter lacks the minimum five papers; no consensus percentage is inferred.
Steffen figure sample counts are dated specimens and archaeological material, not human population counts.
Davis model chronology is a testable proposal, not directly dated movement by a known population.
Gustas reconstructed travel costs are not archaeological observations of routes.
